name: Hear It Before You See It
why_it_works: Taking away the picture makes people listen harder, and the imagination fills the gap with its own image. When the cover art finally sharpens, it either matches what they pictured or surprises them, and both feel like a payoff.

hook.pattern: Black screen, sound first, and a line telling the viewer to turn the sound on before the art appears.
examples: Sound on. You hear it before you see it.
Close your eyes for ten seconds. Then look.

variables.name: artist_name
variables.description: Artist, label, show or team name

variables.name: release_title
variables.description: Name of the single, episode or launch

variables.name: sound_words
variables.description: Three words that describe the sound

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 almost black frame, a single thin glowing line in the center like a quiet audio waveform, deep shadow, subtle film grain
Abstract slow-moving light ribbons pulsing in deep blue and amber on black, smoke-like texture, vertical 9:16, no people, no text
The {{release_title}} cover art heavily blurred, only colors and a rough shape visible, vignette, vertical 9:16
The same {{release_title}} cover art lightly blurred, main shape now clear, same framing, vertical 9:16
The {{release_title}} cover art snapping into sharp focus with a slow parallax push-in and soft light sweep, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: Run the strongest 15 seconds of the original track under the whole reel and keep the screen nearly dark for the first half. Rack the art from blur to focus in steps, timed to the beat drops, so the eyes catch up to the ears.

do_not: Use any audio the artist does not own or license; original music only
Imitate a named artist's sound, voice or cover style
Put lyrics on screen that are not the artist's own
Choose a part of the track without a clear drop or change for the reveal to land on
